expl.summary: Each jet (its 8 hardest particles) is placed on 16 neurons, each a clipped sum of if-statements on jet observables, and each of the five class scores adds some neurons and subtracts others; the formula's accuracy on the validation jets is 0.653. The t score is built mainly on width: it subtracts neuron 13 (girth below 0.148 and λ1 below 0.0164; true tops average 1.08 on it, every other class 3.6-4.5; -48% of the t score) and adds neuron 10 (overall width: girth, girth2, λ1; +26%), so it follows girth and width with rank correlations of 0.917 and 0.913. The q score is mostly neuron 9 (narrow, centred jets, +56%) minus neuron 10 (width, -18%), and follows jet mass and λ1 downwards (rank correlations -0.765 and -0.763). The g score also adds neuron 9 (+22%), and in addition the low-mass, low-angularity neuron 2 (+38%, its largest input) and the broad, small-mass/pT, high-pT neuron 1 (+13%); it subtracts neuron 5 (pT concentrated in the hardest particles, -14%), which is how gluons are separated from quarks. The two boson scores share the elongated, mass/pT-window neuron 7 (+13% of W, +35% of Z) and subtract wide-angle radiation (neuron 3: -16% of W, -23% of Z) and the broad, off-centre neuron 6 (-9% and -14%). They are split mainly by width: the W score adds the compact, centred neuron 11 (+23%) and neuron 0 (+10%), which the Z score does not use, and subtracts the intermediate-width neuron 14 (-9%) and the moderate-width neuron 15 (-7%), while the Z score adds neuron 14 (+6%). Of the particle-mass thresholds that were offered, only two are used, and in small terms: largest subjet-pair mass < 62.55 GeV (half the Higgs mass, neuron 2) and mass > 91.19 GeV (the Z mass, neuron 12); since the jet mass here is that of the 8 hardest particles and does not peak at the W, Z or top masses, these act as ordinary mass cuts.

It rises with eccentricity and falls with planar flow, N2 and τ21 (rank correlations 0.561, -0.561, -0.554, -0.546). W (2.02) and Z (1.98) jets sit highest, far above tops (0.37), gluons (0.15) and quarks (0.15); it is zero for 88.3% of gluons, 89.4% of quarks and 80.4% of tops, but only for 23.9% of W and 22.2% of Z jets.

It rises with angularity (LHA), girth and the distance of the hardest particle from the axis (rank correlations 0.6, 0.596, 0.582). Tops (1.20) and Z jets (1.01) sit highest, gluons (0.73) and W (0.60) in the middle, quarks lowest (0.31); it is zero for 66.8% of quarks and 51.6% of gluons, but only for 15.1% of tops.
1.role: It raises the g score (+13%) and, a little, the Z score (+4%). It does not enter the q, W or t scores.

2.title: low jet mass, low subjet-pair mass and small angularity
2.measures: Its strongest terms subtract for a soft 8th-hardest particle (pT_7 < 53.4 GeV, -12.6%) and for large angularity (LHA > 0.133, -10.5%), and add for mass/pT < 0.108 (+10.1%) and total pT < 813 GeV (+9.4%); a largest subjet-pair mass below 62.55 GeV (half the Higgs mass, one of the offered thresholds) adds +6.5%, while z_7 > 0.0363, very light jets (mass < 36.2 GeV) and max ΔR < 0.251 subtract. Overall it falls with the largest subjet-pair mass and the jet mass of the 8 particles (rank correlations -0.719 and -0.709) and rises with M2 (0.684). Gluons sit highest (3.53), then quarks (2.56), well above W (1.56), Z (1.29) and tops (1.28); it is rarely zero (3.6% of gluons, 22.1% of Z jets).
2.role: It raises the g score, where it is the largest input (+38%). It does not enter the q, W, Z or t scores.

3.title: large mass/pT with pT at 0.2 ≤ ΔR < 0.4 and widely separated subjets

It follows the pT share and the number of particles at 0.2 ≤ ΔR < 0.4 (rank correlations 0.724 and 0.715) and, more weakly, width (0.535). Tops sit far highest (3.76), then gluons (0.89) and quarks (0.46); Z (0.15) and W (0.01) jets are almost never on it (zero for 82.6% of Z and 99.4% of W jets, against 24.1% of tops).
3.role: It lowers the W score (-16%) and the Z score (-23%), and raises the t score only slightly (+2%). It does not enter the g or q scores.

4.title: large mass/pT packed into small e2_sq, small N2 and C2
4.measures: Its two strongest terms are e2_sq < 0.0117 (+28.9%) and (mass/pT)² < 0.0117 (-22.7%): it is on when the jet has (mass/pT)² of at least 0.0117 while e2_sq stays below 0.0117. C2 < 0.0673 and N2 < 0.223 add, girth2 < 0.00868 and a largest 3-subjet distance below 0.234 subtract. It falls with N2, M2, τ21 and D2 (β = 2) (rank correlations -0.628, -0.626, -0.625, -0.593). 4.role: It raises the Z score (+3.5%) and the t score (+4.9%) and lowers the q score (-7.8%). It does not enter the g or W scores.

5.title: pT concentrated in the hardest particles, very narrow core

5.role: It raises the q score (+6%) and lowers the g score (-14%) and the t score (-15%). It does not enter the W or Z scores.

12.role: It does not enter the g, q, W, Z or t scores (its largest weight share is 1.6%), so it has no real effect on the classification.

13.title: girth below 0.148 and λ1 below 0.0164 (not wide)
13.measures: Driven mostly by girth < 0.148 (its strongest term, +29.6%) and λ1 < 0.0164 (+12.3%), both adding when the jet is not wide; e2 < 0.0800 subtracts (-15.1%), as do girth < 0.148 combined with log of total pT < 6.80 and a small e3 with a centred pT centroid. It falls with width, girth2, λ1, girth and mass/pT (rank correlations -0.752, -0.752, -0.751, -0.744, -0.739). Quarks (4.46), W (4.08), Z (3.66) and gluons (3.62) all sit high, tops far lower (1.08, zero for 39.3% of them, against 0.2% of W and Z jets).
13.role: It lowers the t score, where it is the largest input (-48%), and raises the W score (+7%) and the Z score (+7%). It does not enter the g or q scores.

14.title: intermediate width with two subjets more than 0.16 apart
14.measures: Pushed up for girth above 0.0269 and 0.0408, width above 0.00356, a 2-subjet distance above 0.159, e2_sq above 0.0117 and soft-drop mass below 49.9 GeV; pushed down for wider jets (width above 0.00668 and 0.0132, girth2 above 0.00752 and 0.00868, girth above 0.0872), for e2 above 0.0166 and for a soft-drop splitting angle below 0.325. It is therefore largest in a narrow band of width; its correlations with single observables are weak (0.369 with the number of particles). Z jets sit highest (1.31), well above tops (0.29), W (0.15), gluons (0.15) and quarks (0.12); it is zero for 74.9% of W and 32.7% of Z jets.
14.role: It raises the Z score (+6%) and lowers the W score (-9%). It does not enter the g, q or t scores.

15.title: moderate width (below 0.0132) with e2_sq above 0.0117
15.measures: Pushed up for width < 0.0132 (its strongest term, +15.9%) and < 0.0188, e2 < 0.0411, (mass/pT)² < 0.00718 and a 2-subjet distance below 0.159; pushed down for girth < 0.102, e2_sq below 0.00817 and 0.0117, girth2 < 0.00752, mass/pT < 0.131 and a 2-subjet distance below 0.200. So it is on for jets that are not broad but have e2_sq of at least 0.0117. It follows the number of particles at 0.05 ≤ ΔR < 0.1 (0.38) and falls with N2 and τ21 (-0.373, -0.37). Z jets sit highest (0.92), then tops (0.34), gluons (0.17), quarks (0.11) and W (0.10); it is zero for 80.2% of W and 37.2% of Z jets.
15.role: It lowers the W score (-7%) and, slightly, the Z score (-2%). It does not enter the g, q or t scores.

g.title: gluon: low mass, pT spread over many particles
g.measures: High for jets of low mass whose pT is spread over many particles: it rises with M2, z_7 and pT entropy and falls with the pT share of the 5 hardest particles (rank correlations 0.57, 0.556, 0.5, -0.54). It averages 2.02 for g jets, 1.09 for q and 0.88 for t, and is close to zero for W (0.18) and Z (0.11) (AUC 0.83 for gluons against the rest).
g.built_from: Adds the low-mass, low-angularity neuron 2 (+38%, its largest input), the narrow, centred neuron 9 (+22%) and the broad, high-pT neuron 1 (+13%), plus a little of the off-centre neuron 6 (+4.5%); subtracts neuron 5 (pT concentrated in the hardest particles, -14%) and neuron 0 (compact, elongated, -6%).

q.title: quark: narrow, light jet
q.measures: High for narrow, light jets: it falls with jet mass, λ1, width and girth2 (rank correlations -0.765, -0.763, -0.763, -0.763). It averages 1.91 for q jets and 1.35 for g (gluons are its main confusion), 0.19 for W, and is about zero for Z and tops (AUC 0.85 for quarks).
q.built_from: Mostly adds the narrow, centred neuron 9 (+56%); subtracts overall width (neuron 10, -18%) and the large-mass/pT, small-e2_sq neuron 4 (-8%); adds a little of the off-centre neuron 6 (+9%) and of neuron 5 (pT in the hardest particles, +6%).

W.title: W: compact, centred, elongated jet
W.measures: High for compact, centred, elongated jets that are not wider than about width 0.0067; its correlations with single observables are weak (planar flow -0.316, total pT 0.31). It averages 2.55 for W jets and 0.96 for Z, is slightly negative for q (-0.19) and g (-0.45), and strongly negative for t (-2.57) (AUC 0.89).
W.built_from: Adds the compact, centred neuron 11 (+23%, its largest input), the mass/pT-window neuron 7 (+13%), the compact, elongated neuron 0 (+10%) and neuron 13 (not wide, +7%); subtracts wide-angle radiation (neuron 3, -16%), the intermediate-width neuron 14 (-9%), the broad, off-centre neuron 6 (-9%), the moderate-width neuron 15 (-7%) and a little of neurons 9 (-3%) and 8 (-2%).

Z.title: Z: elongated jet of intermediate width
Z.measures: High for elongated jets with mass/pT in the 0.08-0.11 window and an intermediate width; it falls with planar flow and τ21 (β = 2) (rank correlations -0.471 and -0.371). It averages 2.37 for Z jets and 1.50 for W (W is its main confusion), is slightly negative for q (-0.09) and g (-0.29), and strongly negative for t (-2.21) (AUC 0.87).
Z.built_from: Adds the mass/pT-window neuron 7 (+35%, its largest input), neuron 13 (not wide, +7%), the intermediate-width neuron 14 (+6%), neuron 1 (+4%) and neuron 4 (+3.5%); subtracts wide-angle radiation (neuron 3, -23%), the broad, off-centre neuron 6 (-14%) and a little of neurons 9 (-4%) and 15 (-2%).

t.title: top: wide jet
t.measures: High for wide jets: it follows girth, width, girth2, λ1 and LHA with rank correlations of 0.908-0.917. It averages 2.72 for t jets, 0.62 for Z and 0.35 for W, is near zero for g (0.07) and negative for q (-1.25) (AUC 0.91).
t.built_from: Subtracts neuron 13 (girth below 0.148, -48%, its largest input) and adds overall width (neuron 10, +26%); also subtracts neuron 5 (pT concentrated in the hardest particles, -15%) and adds a little of neuron 4 (+4.9%) and of wide-angle radiation (neuron 3, +2.3%).
